title: Helper Functions
story: You're planning a party and the to-do list is overwhelming: send invites, order food, set up decorations, plan activities. Instead of doing everything yourself, you delegate each job to a friend. Functions work the same way — break a big program into small, focused helpers!
why: Breaking programs into small helper functions makes code organized, readable, and easy to change — each function does one job well.
analogy: Helper functions are like delegating chores — one person sets the table, another cooks, another cleans. Each does one job, and together they run the whole household.
expected_output:
Welcome to the Calculator!
Sum is 15
try_it: Split your program into 3 helper functions: one that prints a welcome, one that calculates a sum, and one that prints a goodbye. Call all three from main.
tips: Give each helper function ONE clear job — if you can't describe it in a short sentence, split it further
Name helpers with action words: `print_`, `calc_`, `get_`, `show_` — this makes main read like a story
Keep `main` short — it should read like a checklist of 'what happens', with helpers handling 'how it happens'
common_mistakes: Putting all code in main — if main is longer than 10-15 lines, you probably need helper functions
Making a helper that does too many unrelated things — `calc_and_print_and_save()` is a sign the function should be split
